LAWRENCE ROSEN received his B.A. from Brandeis in 1963 and his Ph.D. from Chicago in 1968. After several years of postdoctoral research at the University of Illinois, University of Chicago, and the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, he returned to the Law School at Chicago where he took his degree in 1974. His main anthropological work has been in North Africa. As a lawyer he has worked on a number of American Indian legal cases. Among his most recent publications are two books: Meaning and Order in Moroccan Society (coauthored with Clifford and Hildred Geertz) and American Indians and the Law (an edited volume). He joined the faculty at Princeton in 1977 after teaching for three years at Duke. He has also served as an Adjunct Professor of Law at Columbia Law School and is a member of the North Carolina and U.S. Supreme Court bars. His only archaeological experience is as an undergraduate
